The worst
Aug 2026 • Family
Terrible food and inattentive staff. We visited this restaurant during our three-week vacation in Vietnam, and it was by far the worst restaurant experience of the entire trip.

The food was bland, poorly presented, and in some cases simply unpleasant. The male waiters spent most of their time looking at their mobile phones instead of paying attention to the guests. We had to remind them to bring our beer, and when they finally brought water, they didn’t provide enough glasses for everyone.

We left almost half of the food untouched because it was either tasteless or simply awful.

We honestly cannot understand how this restaurant can be associated with Michelin. Our advice: save your money and stay away.

Disappointing
Oct 2025 • Friends
Disappointing experience. I do understand that tables inside are not always available on ad hoc visits, so it’s recommended to make a reservation in advance for anyone wanting to visit. Maybe it was an exceptionally busy day, but then it’s the managements responsibility to make sure that there is enough staff available to ensure a proper service or as it’s done in som countries - you just block a certain amount of tables. Some dishes were directly disapproved from the waiter because apparently they were „too dry and not worth it“ which is generally quite questionable from a restaurant which praises itself to be a people’s favourite and on the Michelin guide. The food arrived within a span of 30mins one by one and it was impossible to wait for everyone’s dish to arrive before the other one got cold or soggy. On top of that half of the dishes were basically instantly plated, while the staff was not able to bring all drinks before serving food. The ordered cocktail was tasty, but it was unconventionally made and didn’t remember at all like what was ordered. The food was partially alright, partially was the meat from some dishes still dry and/or unchewable (as even warned by the staff, though there were more meals like that than what we got told). The waiter was nice to ask if he can change or cancel the dish, but sadly after the whole overall experience my appetite was lost. I don’t blame the staff, but the management here - to make that clear

Nice food better Beer but even better staff 😁
Jul 2025 • Couples
I didn’t mind this place. Just so you Westerners are aware appetisers are different, according to my Google search.. “Vietnamese meals are typically served family-style, with all dishes placed on the table at once.” That being said 30 mins after our mains arrived I assumed the crispy spring rolls must have been forgotten about, but then they arrived! They were ok, but my partner didn’t feel safe eating as the inside was very pink. I ate them it’s the next day and I am not sick so stress less! It was a bit confusing to understand what beers I was ordering as I always try the local ones. I had 2 different kinds and the “ST 25” was my favourite. For anyone who doesn’t understand the science of beer head. It came with the perfect amount of head needed to keep the beer fresh and I was very happy with the beer. I took a photo with evidence of beer. The staff are super friendly and I can’t fault them, they were so concerned about my beef being chewy but it wasn’t. Garlic and Chilli flavours were high in the dishes I chose 😁

Rice Field , not again.
Jul 2025 • Couples
On the recommendation of hotel receptionist here reserved a table for two people. Arriving our reservation was apparently not visible but since it was not crowded we could still stay. A slightly more expensive restaurant with lots of choices. The drink was also a bit more expensive. We knew this in advance. They were in fact with a Michelin mention. So expectations were also set. A starter ( 6 Spring Rolls ) for the two of us and both a different main course.
Frank: sparkling water and Belgo beer.
The main course of the lady arrived after 10 minutes and therefore before the main course. At the moment I wanted to ask about the starter , and that was 15 minutes later, the starter and my main course arrived simultaneously. Asking why, my English was apparently not clear or they did not understand and the garçon disappeared again. The dishes themselves were ok but certainly not worthy of a Michelin mention. Simple brasseries often score better, also here in Saigon. The head of the beer was also gone. 
At the settlement they did ask for our opinion on the food. I told them the story then. She was stunned and apologized.

One of the best Vietnamese dinners in Ho Chi Minh!
Dec 2024 • Couples
Wandering around bustling Ho Chi Minh City in search of a Vietnamese restaurant for dinner, we were intrigued by Rice Field , which is located right at the foot of the Bitexo Financial Tower on the opposite side , hard not to find! Original location all in wood with original Vietnamese details , we had dinner on the ground floor , very young waiters in traditional clothes quick and gentle , menu 'extensive at inline prices being recommended on the Michelin Guide .
We ordered more dishes, almost all vegetarian, fantastic fried rolls, other fresh rolls of mixed vegetables, sautéed noodles with tofu and vegetables and fried calamari with vegetables, all great, well presented and hearty dishes, sauces and chilli served separately, however they ask for the degree of spiciness you want. Great idea to bring lettuce to wrap the fried rolls and not get your hands dirty! Really one of the best restaurants we stayed in our three weeks in Vietnam. Recommended! Only note, I would recommend more care in cleaning tables and in the bathroom.

I walked through the still deserted alley in Ho Chi Minh City and found Rice Field on the second floor. I was quickly seated and given a menu. I had read several reviews on Tripadvisor on what to expect and they were spot on except for one thing.

I pushed the spring rolls aside and ordered vegetarian fried rice,

Before the fried rice came out, an employee of the restaurant, that I assumed was the cook, asked me if I liked the spring rolls. I told her I did not like them and she was not interested in knowing why I did not like them.

The fried rice came and I ate it. Nothing special to encourage others to dine at this restaurant.

I asked for the check and the female waiter left to get it for me. While I was waiting, a male waiter came to my table and told me I would have to pay for the vegetarian spring rolls. I paid the bill and promptly left the restaurant.

My first-hand experience at the Rice Field is not to recommend dining here because there are so many other good, friendly restaurants in Ho Chi Minh City where you don't have to put up with rude staff and food you may or may not enjoy.

We had huge expectations but alas the food taste just did not satisfy us!
Jan 2020
After lot of research on TA we short-listed this restaurant for our last dinner of our Vietnam holiday. So, obviously we had lots of expectations. While the location and the interiors of the restaurant are quite good, but the food taste was not up to the mark for us. We did not find the food good. During our holiday in Vietnam, we ate out quite often and must admit that every other place, we had a much better experience. We were a family of 4 (daughters 17 years and 9 years).

We ordered the following. For drinks - Water Melon Juice, House Wine and Coconut Juice. For main course we ordered Grilled Pork Ribs with Salt and Chilli, Braised Codfish with Fish & Garlic Sauce, Grilled Chicken with Herbs and steamed rice. The quantity was also quite average. But that is not the major complaint. It was the taste. We didn't like any of the dishes. I think it was just one of those cases, where nothing clicked. Maybe some of the other dishes would be better. That is the reason why I wrote in details about the dishes so that you can have second thoughts about them. The service was also average. The waiters were not very involved. They were just matter of fact. Instead they could have been more conversant and giving good recommendations, etc. In most other restaurants in Vietnam, we found very conversant and observant waiters who really went out of their ways to make us have a good time and recommended the right stuff. Here there was no such effort made. That was another disappointment.

The bill came to VND 1,034,000. Not cheap. Approximately Malaysia Ringgit 180. Which is a mid range value in Malaysia. Considering the value for money is much more in Vietnam for most things, we would say this amount should have given us a very satisfying meal. But it didn't.

The restaurant is located very near the square near Ho Chi Minh City Hall which is a very happening and buzzing square. That's the only good thing we found because we could easily walk to the square after we finished our dinner here. We went and had good cheesecake ice cream at the square. Sorry forgot the name of the outlet. They were very good ice cream. The restaurant is constructed over 2 levels. The first floor is indoors and the 2nd floor certain part completely outdoor and some parts partially covered. It was quite warm upstairs even if there were air coolers. We preferred to sit upstairs in the semi covered area because the upstairs area was much bigger and more spacious. The first floor indoor was more cramped and had fewer tables. But, now on second thoughts I would recommend that you sit indoors (air conditioned) on the first floor. You might enjoy the food then:)

Well to summarize, Ho Chi Minh City being a bustling city, I am sure we could have found a much better place than this. The food and the service really did not appeal to us.

What we did in Ho Chi Minh City

We arrived on new year's eve evening. Checked into our hotel Hoang Lan Hotel (please see my separate review of this place). Then we went out for dinner to an Indian restaurant called Benaras (please see my separate review of this place). That evening was special dinner and was Bollywood themed. Next day we went sight seeing - Cu Chi Tunnels. Then had lunch at Pizza 4P's. Then went to War Remnants Museum. In the evening we had dinner at this place (Rice Field Restaurant). Then we roamed about at the square in front of Ho Chi Minh City Hall. Then went back to our hotel for our last night at Vietnam. Next morning we went to the airport for our flight back to Malaysia. We quite enjoyed both Cu Chi Tunnels and War Remnants Museum. You can find all detailed reviews on all these places. But overall, we feel HCMC can be avoided compared to Hanoi and Da Nang which we also covered in our Vietnam holiday. HCMC has nothing very different to offer. It is just another city. You can also read my detailed reviews of many restaurants and activities at Hanoi and Da Nang.
